strategy.cardsHeading: Be the Glass Company People Find on Google
strategy.cardsIntro: Each card is one page of the demo: what costs you calls today, and how the demo fixes it.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: The first page people see, and the one Google reads to learn who you are and where you work.
problems: The top of the page says "Custom Residential & Commercial Glass" with no town, and it is not a real headline, so Google cannot tell you are a glass company in Wichita.
Your phone number is plain text at the very bottom of the page, so someone on a phone cannot tap it to call.
fixes: A headline that says glass company in Wichita, KS, right at the top.
Your number is a one-tap call in the top bar and in the footer.
A menu to your shower door, window glass and contact pages, and a card for every service.
cards.alsoAdd: Every page set up behind the scenes so Google and AI tools like ChatGPT know exactly what you do, where you work, and what your customers say.

cards.title: Frameless Shower Doors
cards.why: Shower doors are the work your reviews praise most, and they have no page of their own.
problems: Someone searching "frameless shower doors Wichita" has no page of yours to land on.
The four reviews on your page sit apart from the service they prove.
fixes: A full page for frameless shower doors in Wichita, KS.
Reviews placed beside the point each one proves.
cards.alsoAdd: Pages planned from what Google actually shows for each search, so every page targets something people really look for.

cards.title: Window Glass Replacement
cards.why: Customers buy windows and glass replacements from you, yet the word "window" appears nowhere on your site.
problems: A search for "window glass replacement Wichita" cannot find you, because no page mentions windows.
Your window and aluminum glass door work is invisible, even though one buyer has ordered over 30 windows.
fixes: A page for window glass replacement in Wichita, KS.
Windows, glass replacements and aluminum glass doors named plainly.
cards.alsoAdd: A check of what your competitors offer, so services you didn’t think to mention still get their own pages.

cards.title: Contact
cards.why: The page where interest turns into a call, and where the next step needs to be obvious.
problems: Every "Click for a Quote" button leaves your site for an outside form.
Your email address is plain text, not a link that opens a message.
fixes: A contact page with your number, address and what to have ready.
One tap to call, from every page.
cards.alsoAdd: Call and form tracking that shows which pages and towns your leads come from.

strategy.reportCardHeading: What great glass company websites get right, and how yours measures up.

reportCard.label: Headline says what you do and where
Each money service has its own page
Quote request on your own site
Photos labeled so Google knows what they show

closing.heading: Want a website like this for your business?
closing.text: Your customers already say you show up fast and work clean. You likely do more than we found, so on your onboarding call we confirm every service and detail with you.

onboardingQuestions: Owner and office names and surnames. BBB lists Bryan Chamale (owner) and Karen Chamale (office manager); reviews name "Bryan and Eric". How do they want to be introduced?
Email address to show. The site footer shows an address, but facts.md does not record it, so none is on the demo.
Years in business. BBB says started June 2024; Jordan W.'s review says 7 years with "this family". Is there a predecessor business?
Hours, and whether Saturday is open.
Full list of services: glass repair, tempered and plate glass (BBB categories), mirrors (custom sizes, framed or frameless), glass doors beyond aluminum, specialty glass.
Windows: do they sell and install full replacement windows, or mainly replace the glass? Magnolia W. bought over 30 windows. Which brands, if any?
Do they measure and install every job with their own crew, with no subcontractors?
Towns served beyond Wichita. A customer 1 hour 20 minutes out was served the same day; is there a standard radius?
Is the estimate free, and is the quote usually given the next day (one review)?
Licensing, insurance, warranty on shower doors and windows, and BBB accreditation (the profile says not accredited, A rating).
Financing and any lead-time or install-time promises they are comfortable making.
Logo file, brand colors and real project photos with descriptions.
The 1-star review about broken glass at pickup: do they want a pickup and packaging line added anywhere?
Reviewer names for Vickie and Sherry (Google shows no last initial), so their reviews can be used.
